items.text: Item was created with title "Gamma" and no description, no initiative, no acceptance_allow/deny, and no archive materials. There is effectively zero prior context. Round 1 focuses on eliciting the minimum viable intent so subsequent rounds can converge on a real plan.

items.context: Without a description, we cannot tell whether Gamma is a feature, a bug fix disguised as an execute task, a chore, or a placeholder. Clarifying the primary goal determines which plan sections are load-bearing and whether the item should stay as kind=execute or be converted.

options.label: Ship a new capability / feature
options.rationale: Execute kind fits when the work is a bounded implementation of a known design.

options.label: Fix a defect or regression
options.rationale: If this is a bug, converting to kind=fix unlocks reproduction and root-cause sections in the plan.

options.label: Operational chore (cleanup, upgrade, refactor with no behavior change)
options.rationale: If there is no user-visible change, kind=chore fits better and the plan emphasizes scope boundaries and completion checklist.

options.label: Placeholder — delete this item
options.rationale: "Gamma" reads like a scratch name. If it was created by mistake, the right action is to delete it rather than plan it.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe the intent in freeform.

items.context: spec.json has no acceptance_allow, which means no declared execution boundary. The plan cannot describe the technical context or file layout until this is set. Pick the pattern that best matches where the work will land.

options.label: A single scenario — `scenarios/<scenario>/**`
options.rationale: Most common case for execute items scoped to one product area.

options.label: A specific subtree within a scenario — e.g. `scenarios/<scenario>/api/**`
options.rationale: Tighter boundary when the work is known to be backend-only or UI-only.

options.label: A shared package — e.g. `packages/<pkg>/**`
options.rationale: When the change lives in cross-scenario infrastructure.

options.label: Cross-cutting (multiple scenarios + packages)
options.rationale: Flag this — cross-cutting execute items usually need to be split or promoted to an idea.

options.label: Other / not yet known
options.rationale: Provide the path(s) in freeform or defer until d1 is answered.

items.context: There are 171 existing execute items and many active initiatives. A placeholder name like "Gamma" risks duplicating in-flight work (e.g. naming-related siblings like alpha/beta/gamma/delta). Establishing relationships early prevents redundant work and lets the plan inherit shared context.

options.label: Standalone — no initiative, no dependencies
options.rationale: Simplest case; plan proceeds independently.

options.label: Belongs to an existing initiative (name it in freeform)
options.rationale: Pulls in shared strategy docs via `initiatives context` and aligns decisions with sibling items.

options.label: Depends on one or more existing items (list `kind/name` in freeform)
options.rationale: Dependencies will gate batch-queue ordering; worth capturing now.

options.label: Supersedes / duplicates an existing item (name it in freeform)
options.rationale: If Gamma duplicates other work, preferred action is to close Gamma and contribute context to the existing item.

options.label: Other
options.rationale: Describe the relationship in freeform.

items.topic: Primary success signal / how we will know it is done
items.context: Definition of Done cannot be written until we know what the user will look at to decide the work succeeded. This also drives the Testing Plan section.

options.label: Automated tests passing (unit + integration in the target area)
options.rationale: Typical for backend/API work with clear contracts.

options.label: UI behavior verified manually in a running dev server
options.rationale: Typical for UI-visible changes where tests alone are insufficient.

options.label: CLI / script produces the expected output on a named fixture
options.rationale: Typical for tooling or data-transformation work.

options.label: Document / artifact produced and reviewed
options.rationale: Typical for research-adjacent execute items (reports, RFCs, audits).

options.label: Other / combination
options.rationale: Describe in freeform.

items.context: Sizing sets expectations for how phased the Implementation Strategy should be, and whether this should stay as a single execute item or be split up front.

options.label: XS — trivial, <1 hour of focused work
options.rationale: Plan stays minimal; no phasing.

options.label: S — a few hours, single component
options.rationale: Linear plan with one testing pass.

options.label: M — 1-2 days, one or two components
options.rationale: Light phasing; explicit testing plan.

options.label: L — multi-day, multiple components
options.rationale: Consider splitting into sub-items or promoting to an idea; otherwise use phased plan with dependency notes.

options.label: Unknown
options.rationale: Flag as a risk and resolve in a later round once scope is clearer.

plan_updates: Created plan.md scaffold with all mandatory sections (Purpose, Required Reading, Problem Statement, Scope, Current Technical Context, Target End State, Implementation Strategy, Contract Decisions, Testing Plan, Rollout Checklist, Risks, Non-goals, Definition of Done). Most sections are <!-- TBD --> pending round 1 answers. Populated the Required Reading block, two initial risks (under-specified item and possible duplication), and seeded Phase 1 of the Implementation Strategy as "Clarify intent via workshop round 1".
